newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products-Prices leap on shoulders of NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products-Prices leap on shoulders of NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. spot products prices jumped sharply tracking a strong NYMEX rally late Wednesday, although the gains were partially offset in the Midcontinent Group Three market by slipping differentials, players said.
NYMEX values soared amid vows by OPEC members to stick to output quotas after the group agreed to a rollover of its 25.03 million barrel per day production ceiling.
OPEC ministers, gathered for a summer meeting in Vienna, agreed to roll over their self-imposed production ceiling for six months starting July 1.
NYMEX July heating oil settled 1.42 cents higher, to 52.99 cents a gallon. July gasoline raced 1.29 cents higher, to 56.97 cents.
U.S. MIDCONTINENT:
Differentials on prompt Group Three gasoline eased as much as a half cent by late day amid a sudden spurt of refiner selling and the giddy futures advance, players said.
Conventional unleaded eased to between 4.0 and 4.25 cents over July futures after being traded in the morning for 4.30 cents over, Group Three traders said.

"A bunch of gasoline sellers came out so it decided to get weaker," one trader said. "They had been sitting on barrels, but probably wanted to lighten up because of inventory concerns as we head to the end of the month."
Group Three distillate diffs also eased about 0.25 cent amid the futures rally, traders said, with low sulfur diesel offered at 2.50 cents over the July print.
Diffs were little changed in the Chicago market, however, with conventional unleaded gasoline offered at 0.75 cent over the July print.
U.S. GULF COAST
Prompt regular conventional "M1" gasoline differentials firmed early in the day, boosted by fresh buying interest from two major Gulf Coast refiners, according to traders.

"It was nothing special," one player said, although it was enough to lift prompt differentials about 0.25 cent. Prompt "M1" barrels changed hands at 2.90 cents under the August futures, while end-of-July barrels traded for 3.15 cents under the August futures.
Heating oil differentials also gained modestly, traders said, with prompt barrels talked about 2.10 cents under the July futures, up about 0.15 cent from Tuesday.
Low sulphur diesel offers mimicked that strength, gaining about 0.15 cent to sit near 1.60 cents under the July, according to market players.
NEW YORK HARBOR
New York Harbor differentials ended Wednesday largely unchanged in modest trading activity, according to market watchers.
Prompt heating oil eased to about 0.25 cent under the July NYMEX, about 0.10 cent off late Tuesday levels, though no confirmed deals emerged.
Regular conventional "M2" gasoline, however, remained stable between 2.75 cents and 3.00 cents under the July NYMEX, traders said.
Reformulated "A2" gasoline for prompt delivery in the Harbor was offered at 0.40 cents under the July futures, up about 0.10 cent on the day, though no takers were seen at that level.
